title: LGB+: A Macroeconomic Forecasting Road Test
hypothesis: LGB+ interleaving greedy univariate linear updates with tree boosting improves short-horizon macro forecasts where autoregressive/linear accounting relationships dominate, while retaining nonlinear gains; gains concentrated at h=1 for unemployment and industrial production via linear channel.
data_sources: Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF) Philadelphia Fed
FRED variables CLAIMSx, PERMITS, PCE, etc.
sample: Forecasting exercise for 6 quarterly U.S. macro aggregates: headline CPI inflation, GDP growth, unemployment rate, housing starts log growth, industrial production, term spread (10Y-3M). Predictors from FRED-QD transformed to stationarity, augmented with 4 lags plus MARX moving averages 2,4,8, plus 4 principal components with 4 lags each, standardized to zero mean unit variance over training sample; 37 slowly released variables shifted forward 1 quarter for ragged edge. Direct forecasts at horizons h=1,2,4 quarters with separate models per horizon. Training begins 1961Q2. Evaluation on expanding window re-estimated every 8 quarters (2 years) over pre-COVID 2007Q2--2019Q4 and post-COVID 2022Q1--2025Q1 for GDP/unemployment/industrial production and 2021Q1--2025Q1 for inflation/housing starts/term spread, excluding COVID quarters 2020Q1--2021Q2. Simulation evaluates 8 DGPs (Linear, Product-Log, Mixture, Friedman1, Trig-Log, Soft Radial, Step/U-curve, Rotated Sine) at N=250,500,1000, SNR=0.5,1,2, P=6, 10 replications, test set N=1000.
method: Construct simulation data: draw P=6 predictors uniform [0,1]; define 8 signal functions f(x) as listed; add Gaussian noise calibrated to target SNR 0.5,1,2; generate training sizes N=250,500,1000 and fixed test set N=1000; repeat 10 Monte Carlo replications.

Build empirical predictor panel: take FRED-QD, apply stationarity transformations, add 4 lags and MARX moving averages order 2,4,8; extract 4 principal components from transformed panel and include 4 lags of each PC; standardize all series to zero mean unit variance over training sample; shift 37 slowly released variables forward 1 quarter.

Define targets: quarterly headline CPI inflation, GDP growth, unemployment rate, housing starts log growth, industrial production, change in term spread (10Y-3M); estimate direct forecasting models separately for h=1,2,4.

Train models on expanding window starting 1961Q2, re-estimating every 8 quarters; evaluate out-of-sample on pre-COVID 2007Q2--2019Q4 and post-COVID 2022Q1--2025Q1 (GDP/UR/INDPRO) or 2021Q1--2025Q1 (INFL/HOUST/DSpread). Benchmarks: AR(4), FAAR (4 lags target +2 lags of 4 PCs), Ridge, Kernel Ridge, RF (500 trees, 75% subsampling, min node 5), LightGBM, LGB+ competition (per step fit shallow tree on subsample residuals and greedy univariate OLS on most correlated feature in random subset fraction rho, evaluate L_tree vs L_lin on OOB/validation and advance winner with learning rate eta; ensembling and post-hoc scale calibration y=beta*yhat), LGBA+ alternating (T trees then 1 linear correction with eta_tree/eta_lin on fixed schedule), NN (3x400 ReLU dropout 0.2 Adam), HNN for inflation, TabPFN, SPF median where available.

Compute forecast accuracy: RMSE relative to AR, MAE, rho(1), DM t-stat vs AR; risk-adjusted metrics over squared and absolute errors (Return, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, MaxDD, Edge) as reported in appendix panels A/B; permutation variable importance VI_g = (MSE_permuted - MSE_baseline)/MSE_baseline*100 with decomposition VI_g = VI_linear + VI_trees + C_g where C_g = 200/(n*MSE_base) sum Delta_lin*Delta_tree; dual observation weights via AXIL: yhat_j = sum w_ji y_i with w = w_lin + w_tree; decompose forecasts into linear vs tree contributions.
